title: ADR-0141: D1, the Consequences and exec-plan item 4 say os validate judges neither side of a cross-package binding — false for lookups since #16611
body:
domain:server#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXcN9HaZYSEUdJWEjw

Filing gate: ③ ordered by the maintainer's ruling on #25805. Its letter D ("keep today's behaviour") carries the execution item "ADR-0141 更正单独一张 XS 卡" (decision card, ruling comment on #25805). reach: the ADR text itself. `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, and every later cross-app card reads this ADR as its governing text.
Business reason: ADR-0141 is the governing text for inter-app dependencies. It states that the compile-time tools judge neither side of a cross-package binding. For `Field.lookup` (and a `record_change` trigger's object) that is false. So a reader of the ADR, human or agent, predicts that `os validate` passes a lookup to a dependency's object, when it refuses it. The #25805 analysis already went wrong once on this sentence.
Reader who acts: the ADR lane (Tier H, the maintainer merges), as an XS edit of `docs/adr/0141-inter-app-dependency-declared-checked-before-install.md`.
Dedupe (open AND closed): titles of the last 100 issues and PRs matched against "ADR-0141" and "neither side": 0 hits. #25805 is the parent.

Back-link: #25805 · ⛔ Not a claim. Grading is triage's.

## The sentences (origin/main `492703e14d`)

- D1, L203: "`os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` keep judging neither side of a cross-package binding: a stack there is one app and cannot see its dependencies' objects."
- Consequences, L564: "the compile-time boundary (`os validate` judges neither side of a cross-artifact binding)".
- Execution plan item 4, L730: the docs are to state "that `os validate` cannot see a dependency's objects".

## What the tree does

`packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts` (lines 67-72) refuses an unresolved, non-platform-prefixed reference target with an ERROR. That rule has applied since #16611 (PR #17066). So a lookup to an object that only a dependency provides is judged and refused at build time. It is not left unjudged. The publish gate resolves the dependency closure; the build does not (#25805, letter D: kept as is for now).

## Expected

The three sentences say what the tree does: the compile-time tools judge a cross-package lookup / trigger target and refuse it when the target is not in the stack's own artifact or the platform's names, since they cannot see the dependency's objects. The declared dependency is honoured at the save door and the publish gate, not at build time. That is #25805's open gap, deferred by the maintainer. No behaviour change.
